tool.title: Check a bean is free, then claim it on every copy
tool.description: For one bean: fetch every bean copy, read the last three commits on its file, skip it if another agent committed within the window or its last note is a claim, look for an open PR naming it in every listed repository, and only then set it in-progress with a dated claim note as a plain commit on every copy. A rejected push is fetched, rebased and re-checked, never forced.

inputs.name: id
inputs.description: The bean, full or short id.

inputs.name: copy
inputs.description: A local checkout of a bean copy. Repeat once per copy. Defaults to the current checkout.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.description: A repository whose open PRs are searched for the id. Repeat. Defaults to the copies' repositories.

inputs.name: minePr
inputs.description: The link of an open PR that is the caller's own, when resuming a bean it already holds. Every cloud thread's PR has the same author, so without this any open PR naming the bean is a skip.

inputs.name: as
inputs.description: Which agent is asking, by its name in the agents table. Defaults to `cloud`.

inputs.name: session
inputs.description: The caller's session link, matched against the `Claude-Session:` trailer so a sibling thread of the same agent is told apart. Defaults to $CLAUDE_SESSION_URL.

inputs.name: agents
inputs.description: A JSON file of agents and their commit authors, as in the skill's input schema.

inputs.name: dryRun
inputs.description: Check only; report `would-claim` and write nothing.

outputs.name: check
outputs.description: One of claimed, would-claim, skip-recent-commit, skip-claim-note, skip-open-pr, skip-closed or unknown, with the evidence per copy and the open PRs found. Exit 0 for claimed or would-claim, 1 for a skip, 2 for unknown. Unknown is never reported as free. With --json, `definitions.claimCheck` of schemas/skills/bean-drain/output.schema.json.

outputs.name: result
outputs.description: With --json, the check as one `BeanClaimCheck` record: the state, the evidence per copy and the open PRs found. Programs and BPMN gateways read this; people read `check`.

selection.when: Before any work on a bean, when more than one agent may be draining the same store.
selection.limits: It sees commits and open PRs, not an agent's intent: an agent that works without committing or opening a PR is invisible until it does. One bean per call. `beans:claim` is the right claim when the store has one copy and no other agents drain it.
selection.cost: One fetch and one push per copy, and one paged GitHub REST listing of open PRs per repository.

remedies.none: With no fetch or push, nothing is claimed and the state is unknown. Claim by hand per the skill once the network is back.

With no PR listing the open-work step cannot run, so the state is unknown rather than free. A session with the GitHub MCP server can list open PRs with `list_pull_requests` and search them for the id by hand.

$comment.comment:
The Tool node for the drain's check-then-claim step.

Bean `n7x7`, skill `bean-drain` step 2. The measured case is f1e1 on
2026-10-24: agy opened the tools layer's PR #686 at 07:47:35Z
(https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools/pull/686), a cloud thread
made its first commit at 07:50:08Z and opened #688, and neither had claimed.
Both bean copies said `in-progress` since 2026-10-16 with no newer commit, so
a status check would have said nothing. The open PR said everything, which is
why this tool calls `open-work-lookup` before it claims.

Why not `beans:claim`: `claimOnBranchStore` writes the one copy this checkout
points at, and reads status, not activity. This tool keeps its race safety
(re-read after a rejected push, never force) and adds the activity reads and
the second copy. When the bean store is one copy again, this becomes a thin
wrapper over `beans:claim` plus the lookup.

@module work-plan/tools/bean-claim-check
